sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ nipātite karṇe samare savyasācinā alpāvaśiṣṭāḥ kuravaḥ kim akurvata vai dvija
english: Janamejaya said: When Karṇa had thus been struck down in battle by Savyasācin, and the Kurus were left but few, what then did they do, O brāhmaṇa?

sanskrit: udīryamāṇaṃ ca balaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā suyodhanaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ prāptakālaṃ ca kiṃ prāpadyata kauravaḥ
english: Seeing the host of the Pāṇḍavas surging upward and the hour come upon him, what course did King Suyodhana, the Kaurava, resolve upon?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tad ācakṣva dvijottama na hi tṛpyāmi pūrveṣāṃ śṛṇvānaś caritaṃ mahat
english: This I wish to hear; tell it to me, O best of the twice-born, for I am never sated hearing of the mighty deeds of the ancients.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ karṇe hate rājan dhārtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhanaḥ bhṛśaṃ śokārṇave magno nirāśaḥ sarvato 'bhavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, when Karṇa had been slain, O king, Suyodhana the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra sank deep in an ocean of grief and grew hopeless on every side.

sanskrit: hā karṇa hā karṇa iti śocamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ kṛcchrāt svaśibiraṃ prāyād dhataśeṣair nṛpaiḥ saha
english: Crying again and again "Alas, Karṇa! Alas, Karṇa!" in his sorrow, he made his way with difficulty to his own camp, together with the kings who survived the slaughter.

sanskrit: sa samāśvāsyamāno 'pi hetubhiḥ śāstraniścitaiḥ rājabhir nālabhac charma sūtaputravadhaṃ smaran
english: Though consoled by the kings with reasonings settled in the śāstras, he found no peace, remembering the slaying of the Sūta's son.

sanskrit: sa daivaṃ balavan matvā bhavitavyaṃ ca pārthivaḥ saṃgrāme niścayaṃ kṛtvā punar yuddhāya niryayau
english: Deeming fate all-powerful and what must be inevitable, that prince made his resolve for battle and went forth once more to fight.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā vidhivad rājapuṃgavaḥ raṇāya niryayau rājā hataśeṣair nṛpaiḥ saha
english: Having made Śalya commander of his army with due rites, that bull among kings went forth to war, together with the kings who survived the slaughter.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ babhūva bharataśreṣṭha devāsuraraṇopamam
english: Then a most tumultuous battle arose between the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, O best of the Bhāratas, like the war of gods and asuras.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja kṛtvā kadanam āhave pāṇḍusainyasya madhyāhne dharmarājena pātitaḥ
english: Then, O great king, Śalya, after wreaking havoc in battle among the Pāṇḍava host, was struck down at midday by the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā hatabandhū raṇājirāt apasṛtya hradaṃ ghoraṃ viveśa ripujād bhayāt
english: Then King Duryodhana, his kinsmen slain, withdrew from the field of battle and entered a dreadful lake out of fear born of his enemies.

sanskrit: athāparāhṇe tasyāhnaḥ parivārya mahārathaiḥ hradād āhūya yogena bhīmasenena pātitaḥ
english: Then in the afternoon of that day, surrounded by the great car-warriors and called forth from the lake by a stratagem, he was struck down by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tasmin hate maheṣvāse hataśiṣṭās trayo rathāḥ saṃrabhān niśi rājendra jaghnuḥ pāñcālasainikān
english: When that mighty bowman had been slain, the three car-warriors who remained, in their fury, slew the Pāñcāla soldiers by night, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvāhṇasamaye śibirād etya saṃjayaḥ praviveśa purīṃ dīno duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ
english: Then in the forenoon Saṃjaya, coming from the camp, entered the city wretched, filled with sorrow and grief.

sanskrit: praviśya ca puraṃ tūrṇaṃ bhujāv ucchritya duḥkhitaḥ vepamānas tato rājñaḥ praviveśa niveśanam
english: Having swiftly entered the city, grief-stricken, raising up his arms and trembling, he then entered the dwelling of the king.

sanskrit: ruroda ca naravyāghra hā rājann iti duḥkhitaḥ aho bata vivignāḥ sma nidhanena mahātmanaḥ
english: And he wept aloud, O tiger among men, crying "Alas, O king!" in his grief: "Ah, woe, we are stricken with anguish by the destruction of the great-souled ones."

sanskrit: aho subalavān kālo gatiś ca paramā tathā śakratulyabalāḥ sarve yatrāvadhyanta pārthivāḥ
english: "Ah, how mighty is Time, and how supreme its course, where all those kings, equal in strength to Śakra, were slain!"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva ca puro rājañ janaḥ sarvaḥ sa saṃjayam praruroda bhṛśodvigno hā rājann iti sasvaram
english: And the moment they saw Saṃjaya before them, O king, all the people, sorely agitated, wailed loudly, crying "Alas, O king!"

sanskrit: ākumāraṃ naravyāghra tat puraṃ vai samantataḥ ārtanādaṃ mahac cakre śrutvā vinihataṃ nṛpam
english: That whole city, O tiger among men, down to its children, raised on every side a great cry of anguish when it heard the king had been slain.

sanskrit: dhāvataś cāpy apaśyac ca tatra trīn puruṣarṣabhān naṣṭacittān ivonmattāñ śokena bhṛśapīḍitān
english: And he saw there three bulls among men running about, like men robbed of their senses, like madmen, sorely afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: tathā sa vihvalaḥ sūtaḥ praviśya nṛpatikṣayam dadarśa nṛpatiśreṣṭhaṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram
english: Then that overwhelmed sūta, entering the dwelling of the king, beheld the best of kings, the lord whose eye was wisdom.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā cāsīnam anaghaṃ samantāt parivāritam snuṣābhir bharataśreṣṭha gāndhāryā vidureṇa ca
english: And he saw the sinless one seated, surrounded on every side by his daughters-in-law, by Gāndhārī, and by Vidura, O best of the Bhāratas,

sanskrit: tathānyaiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca jñātibhiś ca hitaiṣibhiḥ tam eva cārthaṃ dhyāyantaṃ karṇasya nidhanaṃ prati
english: and by other friends and kinsmen who wished him well, while he brooded upon that very matter — the death of Karṇa.

sanskrit: rudann evābravīd vākyaṃ rājānaṃ janamejaya nātihṛṣṭamanāḥ sūto bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā
english: Weeping still, the sūta, his mind far from glad, addressed these words to the king, O Janamejaya, in a voice choked with tears:

sanskrit: saṃjayo 'haṃ naravyāghra namas te bharatarṣabha madrādhipo hataḥ śalyaḥ śakuniḥ saubalas tathā ulūkaḥ puruṣavyāghra kaitavyo dṛḍhavikramaḥ
english: "I am Saṃjaya, O tiger among men; homage to you, O bull of the Bhāratas. Śalya, lord of the Madras, is slain, and Śakuni, son of Subala, and Ulūka, O tiger among men, the son of the gambler, of steadfast valor."

sanskrit: saṃśaptakā hatāḥ sarve kāmbojāś ca śakaiḥ saha mlecchāś ca pārvatīyāś ca yavanāś ca nipātitāḥ
english: "The saṃśaptakas are all slain, and the Kāmbojas together with the Śakas; the mlecchas too, the mountain-dwellers, and the Yavanas have been struck down."

sanskrit: prācyā hatā mahārāja dākṣiṇātyāś ca sarvaśaḥ udīcyā nihatāḥ sarve pratīcyāś ca narādhipa rājāno rājaputrāś ca sarvato nihatā nṛpa
english: "The men of the east are slain, O great king, and those of the south entirely; all those of the north are killed, and those of the west, O lord of men; kings and princes have been slain on every side, O king."

sanskrit: duryodhano hato rājan yathoktaṃ pāṇḍavena ca bhagnasaktho mahārāja śete pāṃsuṣu rūṣitaḥ
english: "Duryodhana is slain, O king, as foretold by the Pāṇḍava; his thighs broken, O great king, he lies in the dust, smeared over with it."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno hato rājañ śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ uttamaujā yudhāmanyus tathā rājan prabhadrakāḥ
english: "Dhṛṣṭadyumna is slain, O king, and the unconquered Śikhaṇḍin, Uttamaujas and Yudhāmanyu too, O king, and the Prabhadrakas."

sanskrit: pāñcālāś ca naravyāghrāś cedayaś ca niṣūditāḥ tava putrā hatāḥ sarve draupadeyāś ca bhārata karṇaputro hataḥ śūro vṛṣaseno mahābalaḥ
english: "The Pāñcālas, those tigers among men, and the Cedis are destroyed; all your sons are slain, and the sons of Draupadī, O Bhārata; the heroic son of Karṇa, the mighty Vṛṣasena, is slain."

sanskrit: narā vinihatāḥ sarve gajāś ca vinipātitāḥ rathinaś ca naravyāghra hayāś ca nihatā yudhi
english: "All the foot-soldiers are slain and the elephants struck down; the car-warriors too, O tiger among men, and the horses have been killed in the battle."

sanskrit: kiṃciccheṣaṃ ca śibiraṃ tāvakānāṃ kṛtaṃ vibho pāṇḍavānāṃ ca śūrāṇāṃ samāsādya parasparam
english: "Little is left of the camp of your men, O lord, nor of the heroes of the Pāṇḍavas, after they clashed with one another."

sanskrit: prāyaḥ strīśeṣam abhavaj jagat kālena mohitam sapta pāṇḍavataḥ śeṣā dhārtarāṣṭrās tathā trayaḥ
english: "The world, deluded by Time, has come down well-nigh to women alone; seven remain on the Pāṇḍava side, and of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's, three."

sanskrit: te caiva bhrātaraḥ pañca vāsudevo 'tha sātyakiḥ kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca drauṇiś ca jayatāṃ varaḥ
english: "Those are the five brothers, then Vāsudeva and Sātyaki; and Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman, and Droṇa's son, best of the victorious."

sanskrit: tavāpy ete mahārāja rathino nṛpasattama akṣauhiṇīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ sametānāṃ janeśvara ete śeṣā mahārāja sarve 'nye nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: "These car-warriors are yours, O great king, O best of kings; of all the akṣauhiṇīs gathered together, O lord of men, these alone remain, O great king; all the others have gone to destruction."

sanskrit: kālena nihataṃ sarvaṃ jagad vai bharatarṣabha duryodhanaṃ vai purataḥ kṛtvā vairasya bhārata
english: "By Time the whole world has been slain, O bull of the Bhāratas, with Duryodhana set foremost in the enmity, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacaḥ krūraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ nipapāta mahārāja gatasattvo mahītale
english: Hearing these cruel words, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, fell to the ground, O great king, his spirit gone.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmau viduro 'pi mahāyaśāḥ nipapāta mahārāja rājavyasanakarśitaḥ
english: When he had fallen to the earth, Vidura too, of great renown, fell down, O great king, worn with grief at the king's calamity.

sanskrit: gāndhārī ca nṛpaśreṣṭha sarvāś ca kuruyoṣitaḥ patitāḥ sahasā bhūmau śrutvā krūraṃ vacaś ca tāḥ
english: And Gāndhārī, O best of kings, and all the women of the Kurus fell suddenly to the earth on hearing those cruel words.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃjñaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau tadāsīd rājamaṇḍalam pralāpayuktā mahatī kathā nyastā paṭe yathā
english: That whole royal circle then lay senseless, fallen to the earth, like a great tale full of lamentation set down upon a painted scroll.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇa tu tato rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ śanair alabhata prāṇān putravyasanakarśitaḥ
english: Then with much difficulty King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, slowly regained his breath, worn with grief at the loss of his sons.

sanskrit: labdhvā tu sa nṛpaḥ saṃjñāṃ vepamānaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ udīkṣya ca diśaḥ sarvāḥ kṣattāraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Having regained his senses, that king, trembling and sorely grieved, looked toward all the quarters and spoke these words to the Steward:

sanskrit: vidvan kṣattar mahāprājña tvaṃ gatir bharatarṣabha mamānāthasya subhṛśaṃ putrair hīnasya sarvaśaḥ evam uktvā tato bhūyo visaṃjño nipapāta ha
english: "O learned Steward, of great wisdom, you are my refuge, O bull of the Bhāratas — mine, who am forlorn, utterly bereft of all my sons." Having spoken thus, he again fell down senseless.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāndhavā ye 'sya ke cana śītais tu siṣicus toyair vivyajur vyajanair api
english: Seeing him thus fallen, such kinsmen of his as were near sprinkled him with cool waters and fanned him with fans.

sanskrit: sa tu dīrgheṇa kālena pratyāśvasto mahīpatiḥ tūṣṇīṃ dadhyau mahīpālaḥ putravyasanakarśitaḥ niḥśvasañ jihmaga iva kumbhakṣipto viśāṃ pate
english: After a long while that lord of the earth, regaining his composure, brooded in silence, the king worn with grief at the loss of his sons, hissing like a serpent thrust into a jar, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: saṃjayo 'py arudat tatra dṛṣṭvā rājānam āturam tathā sarvāḥ striyaś caiva gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: Saṃjaya too wept there, seeing the king so stricken, as did all the women, and the illustrious Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tato dīrgheṇa kālena viduraṃ vākyam abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭro naravyāghro muhyamāno muhur muhuḥ
english: Then after a long while Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that tiger among men, swooning again and again, spoke these words to Vidura:

sanskrit: gacchantu yoṣitaḥ sarvā gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī tatheme suhṛdaḥ sarve bhraśyate me mano bhṛśam
english: "Let all the women go, and the illustrious Gāndhārī, and likewise all these friends; my mind is utterly giving way."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ kṣattā tāḥ striyo bharatarṣabha visarjayām āsa śanair vepamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the Steward, O bull of the Bhāratas, gently dismissed those women, himself trembling again and again.

sanskrit: niścakramus tataḥ sarvās tāḥ striyo bharatarṣabha suhṛdaś ca tataḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā rājānam āturam
english: Then all those women went out, O bull of the Bhāratas, and all the friends as well, having seen the king so stricken.

sanskrit: tato narapatiṃ tatra labdhasaṃjñaṃ paraṃtapa avekṣya saṃjayo dīno rodamānaṃ bhṛśāturam
english: Then, O scorcher of foes, Saṃjaya, wretched, looking upon that lord of men who had regained his senses there, weeping and sorely afflicted,

sanskrit: prāñjalir niḥśvasantaṃ ca taṃ narendraṃ muhur muhuḥ samāśvāsayata kṣattā vacasā madhureṇa ha
english: with joined palms — and the Steward too — comforted with gentle words that lord of men, who sighed again and again.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca visṛṣṭāsv atha nārīṣu dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ vilalāpa mahārāja duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ gataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the women had been dismissed, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, lamented, O great king, passing from grief to deeper grief.

sanskrit: sadhūmam iva niḥśvasya karau dhunvan punaḥ punaḥ vicintya ca mahārāja tato vacanam abravīt
english: Sighing as if with smoke, wringing his hands again and again, and reflecting, O great king, he then spoke these words:

sanskrit: aho bata mahad duḥkhaṃ yad ahaṃ pāṇḍavān raṇe kṣemiṇaś cāvyayāṃś caiva tvattaḥ sūta śṛṇomi vai
english: "Ah, woe, this is great sorrow, that I hear from you, O sūta, that the Pāṇḍavas are safe and unscathed in the battle."

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ mama yac chrutvā nihatān putrān dīryate na sahasradhā
english: "Surely my heart is most hard, made of the very stuff of adamant, since on hearing my sons slain it does not burst into a thousand pieces."

sanskrit: cintayitvā vacas teṣāṃ bālakrīḍāṃ ca saṃjaya adya śrutvā hatān putrān bhṛśaṃ me dīryate manaḥ
english: "Recalling their speech and their childhood play, O Saṃjaya, now on hearing my sons slain, my mind is utterly torn asunder."

sanskrit: andhatvād yadi teṣāṃ tu na me rūpanidarśanam putrasnehakṛtā prītir nityam eteṣu dhāritā
english: "Though through my blindness I had no sight of their forms, yet the affection born of a father's love for them I held ever in my heart."

sanskrit: bālabhāvam atikrāntān yauvanasthāṃś ca tān aham madhyaprāptāṃs tathā śrutvā hṛṣṭa āsaṃ tathānagha
english: "As they passed beyond childhood, and stood in youth, and came to the prime of life, on hearing of it I rejoiced, O sinless one."

sanskrit: tān adya nihatāñ śrutvā hṛtaiśvaryān hṛtaujasaḥ na labhe vai kva cic chāntiṃ putrādhibhir abhiplutaḥ
english: "Hearing them now slain, their sovereignty stripped away, their splendor stripped away, I find no peace anywhere, overwhelmed by sorrow for my sons."

sanskrit: ehy ehi putra rājendra mamānāthasya sāṃpratam tvayā hīno mahābāho kāṃ nu yāsyāmy ahaṃ gatim
english: "Come, come, my son, O lord of kings, to me who am now forlorn; bereft of you, O mighty-armed one, to what refuge shall I go?"

sanskrit: gatir bhūtvā mahārāja jñātīnāṃ suhṛdāṃ tathā andhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca māṃ vīra vihāya kva nu gacchasi
english: "Having been the refuge, O great king, of kinsmen and friends alike, where do you go, O hero, abandoning me, blind and old?"

sanskrit: sā kṛpā sā ca te prītiḥ sā ca rājan sumānitā kathaṃ vinihataḥ pārthaiḥ saṃyugeṣv aparājitaḥ
english: "That tenderness of yours, that affection, and that high honor you bore, O king — how were you, unconquered in battles, slain by the Pārthas?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvaṃ pṛthivīpālān bhuktvā tāta samāgatān śeṣe vinihato bhūmau prākṛtaḥ kunṛpo yathā
english: "How is it that you, having enjoyed the homage of the assembled lords of the earth, my child, now lie slain upon the ground like some common, paltry king?"

sanskrit: ko nu mām utthitaṃ kālye tāta tāteti vakṣyati mahārājeti satataṃ lokanātheti cāsakṛt
english: "Who now, when I rise at dawn, will say to me 'Father, father,' and ever 'Great king,' and again and again 'Lord of the world'?"

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ca māṃ kaṇṭhe snehenāklinnalocanaḥ anuśādhīti kauravya tat sādhu vada me vacaḥ
english: "Embracing me about the neck, his eyes moist with affection, who will say 'Command me,' O Kaurava — speak to me that good word!"

sanskrit: nanu nāmāham aśrauṣaṃ vacanaṃ tava putraka bhūyasī mama pṛthvīyaṃ yathā pārthasya no tathā
english: "Did I not surely hear your word, my dear son: 'This earth of mine is greater than the Pārtha's, not theirs'?"

sanskrit: bhagadattaḥ kṛpaḥ śalya āvantyo 'tha jayadrathaḥ bhūriśravāḥ somadatto mahārājo 'tha bāhlikaḥ
english: "Bhagadatta, Kṛpa, Śalya, the lord of the Avantis, and Jayadratha; Bhūriśravas, Somadatta, and the great king Bāhlika;"

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā ca bhojaś ca māgadhaś ca mahābalaḥ bṛhadbalaś ca kāśīśaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ
english: "Aśvatthāman, and the Bhoja, and the mighty king of Magadha; Bṛhadbala, the lord of Kāśi, and Śakuni the son of Subala;"

sanskrit: mlecchāś ca bahusāhasrāḥ śakāś ca yavanaiḥ saha sudakṣiṇaś ca kāmbojas trigartādhipatis tathā
english: "The mlecchas in their many thousands, the Śakas together with the Yavanas, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, and the lord of the Trigartas;"

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ pitāmahaś caiva bhāradvājo 'tha gautamaḥ śrutāyuś cācyutāyuś ca śatāyuś cāpi vīryavān
english: "Bhīṣma the grandsire, and Bhāradvāja, and the Gautama; Śrutāyus and Acyutāyus, and the valiant Śatāyus;"

sanskrit: jalasaṃdho 'thārśyaśṛṅgī rākṣasaś cāpy alāyudhaḥ alaṃbuso mahābāhuḥ subāhuś ca mahārathaḥ
english: "Jalasaṃdha, then Ārśyaśṛṅgi, and the rākṣasa Alāyudha; the mighty-armed Alambusa, and Subāhu the great car-warrior —"

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo rājāno rājasattama madartham udyatāḥ sarve prāṇāṃs tyaktvā raṇe prabho
english: "These and many other kings, O best of kings, all stood ready for my sake, giving up their lives in battle, O lord."

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ madhye sthito yuddhe bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ yodhayiṣyāmy ahaṃ pārthān pāñcālāṃś caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: "'Standing in their midst in the war, surrounded by my brothers, I shall make battle against the Pārthas and against all the Pāñcālas,'"

sanskrit: cedīṃś ca nṛpaśārdūla draupadeyāṃś ca saṃyuge sātyakiṃ kuntibhojaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ ca ghaṭotkacam
english: "'and the Cedis, O tiger among kings, and the sons of Draupadī in the encounter, Sātyaki and Kuntibhoja, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca' —

sanskrit: eko 'py eṣāṃ mahārāja samarthaḥ saṃnivāraṇe samare pāṇḍaveyānāṃ saṃkruddho hy abhidhāvatām kiṃ punaḥ sahitā vīrāḥ kṛtavairāś ca pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: "'Even one of these, O great king, is able to ward off in battle the Pāṇḍava host charging in fury; how much more these heroes together, sworn in enmity to the Pāṇḍavas!'"

sanskrit: atha vā sarva evaite pāṇḍavasyānuyāyibhiḥ yotsyanti saha rājendra haniṣyanti ca tān mṛdhe
english: "'Or else all of these will fight against the followers of the Pāṇḍava, O lord of kings, and will slay them in the fray.'"

sanskrit: karṇas tv eko mayā sārdhaṃ nihaniṣyati pāṇḍavān tato nṛpatayo vīrāḥ sthāsyanti mama śāsane
english: "'Karṇa alone, together with me, will slay the Pāṇḍavas; then the heroic kings will abide under my command.'"

sanskrit: yaś ca teṣāṃ praṇetā vai vāsudevo mahābalaḥ na sa saṃnahyate rājann iti mām abravīd vacaḥ
english: "'And he who is their leader, the mighty Vāsudeva, does not gird himself for arms, O king' — such was the word he spoke to me."

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ vadataḥ sūta bahuśo mama saṃnidhau yuktito hy anupaśyāmi nihatān pāṇḍavān mṛdhe
english: "As he spoke thus to me many times in my presence, O sūta, by his reasoning I did indeed foresee the Pāṇḍavas slain in the fray."
